name: Brave
statusNote: Actively developed with desktop and mobile releases.

availability.cpuNotes: Supported architecture depends on the platform release.
availability.installMethod: Official installer, package repository, or app store.

foundation.codeLicense: Open-source Chromium-derived browser with Brave proprietary services

telemetry.note: Brave documents privacy-preserving product analytics and opt-out controls.

trackerBlocking.note: Brave Shields blocks ads and trackers by default with configurable lists.

privacy.privateWindows: Private windows omit local history; optional Tor windows route traffic through Tor but have distinct limitations.

vpnOrProxy.note: Brave offers a paid VPN and a Tor-window mode in supported desktop releases.

manifestV2.note: Compatibility follows Chromium's changing extension API support.

extensions.limitations: Chrome extensions generally work, but Brave Shields can alter extension or site behavior.

nativeContentBlocking.note: Shields is native and uses filter lists for content blocking.

verticalTabs.note: Brave documents vertical tabs in its tab features.

tabTrees.note: Tree Tabs ship behind a flag and a Tabs setting, off by default.

profiles.note: Profiles or equivalent browser identities are available.

splitView.note: A native Split View is documented in the tab menu.

sidebar.note: Brave Sidebar provides pinned sites and browser tools.

readerMode.note: Brave Reader Mode is built in.

sync.note: Brave Sync synchronizes supported browser data without an account.

translation.note: A built-in translation feature is documented.

pwa.note: Progressive web apps are supported by the Chromium install flow.

iosEngine.note: Apple permits alternative engines in the EU and Japan under entitlement; no non-WebKit build ships in the App Store.

assistant.note: Leo provides a built-in assistant surface.

summarization.note: Leo documents page or multi-tab summarisation.

agenticActions.note: Brave documents its browser agent as off by default and behind an opt-in feature flag.

aiSearch.note: Leo documents AI-assisted answers in search or the address bar.

contentGeneration.note: Leo documents text or image generation.

modelChoice.note: Leo documents a choice of models or local model support.

aiPrivacyControls.note: Leo documents retention, training or kill-switch controls.

crossTabContext.note: Leo documents awareness of multiple tabs or history.

voiceMultimodal.note: Leo documents voice or image interaction.

dataSaver.note: No documented data-saving or compression mode.

mobileExtensions.note: Extension support on mobile is not documented.

downloadManager.note: A built-in download manager is not documented.

backgroundMedia.note: Background or picture-in-picture playback is not documented.

webPush.note: Web push support is not documented.
